messages:
deploy-bot: Starting progressive rollout: redwood-base-8k v4.2.1 -> prod (canary 5% on cluster-eu-1) at 2109876543
Lucy (ML Eng): FYI this bundle includes a tokenizer tweak and new weightset compiled with quant-opt-3. double-checked checksums locally.
Adele (Support): Noted, tagging support for any customer noise.
Incident Bot: Paging oncall: @Mia (oncall) - increased 5xx observed for model redwood-base-8k in eu-1 canary group (>= 1.5% error rate).
Mia (oncall): Got the page. Looking at logs. Can someone post canary logs?
Raj SRE: Jumping in. Early signals: latency + error spike coincident with canary start. 502 from model gateway, tokenizer errors in logs: `TokenizerError: unknown token <0xEF> at pos 0` repeated. Also seeing weight checksum mismatch warnings: `weights/part-3 checksum mismatch expected abc123 got def456`.
Lucy (ML Eng): that's bad. The build step should have aborted on checksum mismatch. I'm pulling the rollout artifact IDs now.
Mia (oncall): How widespread? Only canary?
Raj SRE: So far only cluster-eu-1 canary nodes (5% traffic). No other regions. Error rate ~2.1% in canary, latency p95 increased from 180ms -> 2.1s.
Adele (Support): Customer-facing alerts? Any user-facing errors logged?
Lucy (ML Eng): Logs show tokenization failing for some requests leading to upstream 502. The tokenizer binary in artifact v4.2.1 appears to be built against the wrong protobuf schema. This would explain the unknown token bytes and could cascade to model runtime expecting different kv-cache format.
Incident Bot: Escalation: Severity=high if >1% errors and user-facing.
Carlos (PM): Customer impact estimate? Which customers routed to eu-1?
Adele (Support): Initial look: a handful of enterprise customers pinned to eu-1 for data residency; some chat threads showing aborted responses. I'll open a customer impact tracker.
Mia (oncall): We should flip the killswitch for this rollout and stop canary traffic. Which flag controls routing?
Raj SRE: Feature flag `ff_rollout/redwood-base-8k/v4.2.1` controls weighted routing. I can force-toggle to 0% for eu-1. Command: `rwoodctl flags set ff_rollout/redwood-base-8k/v4.2.1 --env prod --weight 0 --region eu-1`
Lucy (ML Eng): Also we should prevent further pod restarts pulling v4.2.1. Recommend disabling the deploy pipeline trigger temporarily.
Mia (oncall): Please run the kill now, Raj. I'm going to put a temporary alert suppression for eu-1 to avoid noisy pages while we stabilize.
Raj SRE: Running kill-switch now...
Raj SRE: `rwoodctl flags set ff_rollout/redwood-base-8k/v4.2.1 --env prod --weight 0 --region eu-1` -> OK 200. Disabled canary routing to v4.2.1 in eu-1.
Incident Bot: Action logged by Raj SRE: kill-switch toggled at 2109876920
Lucy (ML Eng): Thanks. We're seeing error rates drop back to baseline within a minute. Tokenizer errors stop in logs.
Adele (Support): Notifying affected customers: short note posted to the pinned tracker: "We briefly routed a release that caused aborted responses for a subset of EU customers. We've halted the rollout and are investigating. No data loss, only transient failed responses."
Carlos (PM): Good. Let's decide rollback vs fix. If artifact had wrong tokenizer binary, patch and re-run CI to verify checksums, but we need guaranteed fix.
Lucy (ML Eng): I recommend rolling back the canary entirely to v4.2.0 and disabling auto-rollout until we have deterministic checksum verification in pipeline. I will run a full reproduce in staging with the exact packaging steps.
Mia (oncall): Agreed. Raj, can you run a rollback for the cluster-level canary and block further v4.2.1 promotions?
Raj SRE: Initiating rollback command:```
rwoodctl rollout rollback --model redwood-base-8k --from-version v4.2.1 --to-version v4.2.0 --scope region=eu-1 --force
```
Raj SRE: Rollback in progress -> pods draining, routing switched. Confirming post-rollback health checks.
Incident Bot: Rollback completed at 2109877050 by Raj SRE.
Mia (oncall): Health checks green, error rate back to baseline, latencies normalized. I'm keeping the suppression window open for 30m to monitor.
Lucy (ML Eng): I've started a deep-dive: reproducer run shows build system occasionally picking up an old tokenizer binary from a shared cache when parallel builds overlap. I'll open a PR to pin artifact hashes and fail the build on mismatch.
Adele (Support): Customer comms: Sent out targeted notices to 4 enterprise accounts; created status page incident. No escalation to legal yet.
Carlos (PM): Please prepare incident summary: timeline, root cause hypothesis (packaging cache contaminates tokenizer binary leading to checksum mismatch), impact (5% canary, ~2% errors for affected requests, enterprise customers in eu-1 briefly experienced aborted responses), mitigation (kill-switch, rollback), follow-ups (CI hardening, checksum gating, audit of artifact store).
Mia (oncall): I'm handing off to Lucy for next steps and postmortem. @Lucy (ML Eng) will lead the RCA. I'm logging the handoff: oncall -> Lucy at 2109877300.
Lucy (ML Eng): Acknowledged. I'll convene a postmortem and include Raj and Adele. Will post a draft in #postmortems in 48 hours.
Mia (oncall): Leaving monitoring for the next 30m then ending shift. If anything flares, ping me. :thumbsup:
Incident Bot: Incident severity downgraded to low at 2109877600. Follow-up tasks assigned: `RCA-1234` to Lucy, `CI-987` to Eng Infra.
Adele (Support): Adding notes to customer tracker and closing live communications once status page updated.
Carlos (PM): Thanks team. Good containment.
Lucy (ML Eng): Will also add a test in the packaging pipeline to validate tokenizer ABI compatibility.
Raj SRE: Will add a guard to prevent parallel-build cache contamination.
Mia (oncall): Closing thread, handoff recorded."
